summary: Serverless/BaaS architecture: Firebase serving React + Vite (SPA) (web) + React Native (Expo) for Android + iOS + Tauri (desktop), hosted on Cloudflare (Workers static assets / Pages). Estimated $0-2/month (within the $200 budget).

architecture_rationale.text: Firebase provides data, auth and APIs as managed services; custom logic runs as functions, so there is no server fleet to operate. Over-engineering guard: microservices rejected: 2 engineer(s), no DevOps cannot absorb the operational overhead.

frontend.choice: React + Vite (SPA) (web) + React Native (Expo) for Android + iOS + Tauri (desktop)
frontend.justification: Web - React + Vite (SPA): Chosen because team already works in typescript (team.languages); strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=3; shares React/TypeScript skills and code with the React Native (Expo) app; rich client-side interactivity for a web_app. Mobile - React Native (Expo): Chosen because team already works in typescript (team.languages); one codebase ships both Android and iOS (project.platforms); strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=3; on-device SQLite storage and background sync for offline_support=true. Desktop - Tauri: Chosen because team already works in typescript (team.languages); strong cost efficiency (5/5) with priorities.cost=3; strong performance (5/5) with priorities.performance=3; reuses the React + Vite (SPA) web UI code on the desktop.

alternatives.why_not: React + Vite scores higher on platform coverage (fit 8.1 vs 8.6).
WebView storage is a weaker base for offline-first data. React Native scores higher on maintainability and performance (fit 7.0 vs 9.2).
Tauri scores higher on performance and cost (fit 7.2 vs 8.8).

tradeoffs: Routing/data fetching choices left to the team
Some native modules need custom development builds
Native logic needs Rust
WebView rendering differs per OS

database.justification: Chosen because Firebase is built on Cloud Firestore; strong scalability (5/5) with priorities.scalability=3; strong time-to-market (5/5) with priorities.time_to_market=3; client SDKs sync offline writes. warnings.message: Scope (~18.0 feature points: 4 platform(s), web_app domain, requirements) far exceeds capacity (2 intermediate engineer(s) x 3 weeks). Ship one platform first.
4 client platforms in 3 weeks: cross-platform code sharing is assumed; consider launching on one platform first.
Offline + realtime editing implies CRDT-style merging on reconnect.
Offline writes need a conflict policy: client-generated UUIDs, server-authoritative merge or per-field last-write-wins, and idempotent sync endpoints.
Cloud Firestore is proprietary; migrating away later means rewriting the data layer.
Firebase (Firestore + Auth + Functions) is proprietary; migrating away later means rewriting the data layer.
